data.name: Taiwan
data.summary: Taiwan taxes individuals on Taiwan-source income at up to 40%. Foreign income, including foreign capital gains and dividends, is reached only by the 20% alternative minimum tax (income basic tax), which applies when foreign income is TWD 1 million or more and basic income exceeds TWD 7.5 million; for a family of this size that is close to a flat 20%. Taiwan listed-share gains are exempt (0.3% transaction tax), and Taiwan dividends cost up to 28%. Estate and gift tax (10%-20%) reaches only Taiwan-situs property of foreign nationals. There is no wealth tax and no US tax treaty.

regimes.name: Taiwan resident
regimes.description: Taiwan-source income at 5%-40%; foreign income only through the 20% income basic tax above TWD 7.5 million; estate tax on Taiwan assets only for foreigners.
regimes.eligibility: Foreigners are resident if present 183 days or more in a calendar year.

capital_gains.summary: Taiwan taxes individuals' Taiwan-source income at 5%-40%. Gains on Taiwan securities are exempt from income tax (a 0.3% securities transaction tax applies to share sales). Foreign-source income, including gains on foreign securities and foreign property, is outside the regular income tax but enters the alternative minimum tax (income basic tax, IBT) at 20% once a resident's foreign income is TWD 1 million or more and basic income exceeds TWD 7.5 million, with a credit for foreign tax. Taiwan real estate acquired from 2016 is under the consolidated house and land income tax: 45% (2 years or less), 35% (2-5), 20% (5-10), 15% (over 10 years); a self-used home qualifies for TWD 4 million exemption and 10% above it.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: IBT: TWD 7.5 million deduction from basic income (2025 filing figure); foreign income under TWD 1 million is excluded entirely.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: IBT is payable only to the extent it exceeds regular income tax. For the family's scale (foreign income far above TWD 7.5 million) the effective rate approaches 20%. Gains on certain unlisted/privately placed securities are IBT add-back items.

sources.title: Taiwan - Individual - Taxes on personal income
Amendments to the consolidated house and land income tax (House and Land Tax 2.0)

open_questions: Treatment of gains on unlisted Taiwan shares under IBT not verified.
IBT deduction for 2026 income (TWD 7.5 million used) may be indexed.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Foreign gains: 20% IBT. Domestic listed: income-tax exempt, 0.3% securities transaction tax on proceeds = 0.6% of the gain assuming the gain is half the proceeds. Private business sale (unlisted Taiwan company): assumed to fall into IBT at 20% (low confidence). Local real estate held over 10 years: 15%. Headline 45% = short-holding house and land rate.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Securities gains remain exempt even for frequent traders (general knowledge); property dealing businesses are taxed under the house and land rules.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: House and land tax rates fall with holding period (above).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign income is taxed only through IBT (20%) and only for residents (183 days or domiciled).

dividends.summary: Taiwan dividends of resident individuals are either included in consolidated income (up to 40%) with an 8.5% credit capped at TWD 80,000, or taxed separately at 28%. Foreign dividends are foreign-source income, outside regular tax but included in IBT at 20% (same thresholds as above) with credit for foreign tax.
dividends.important_exceptions: Dividend options from the 2018 integrated-system reform (general knowledge; PwC page opened does not list them).

sources.title: Taiwan - Individual - Taxes on personal income
Taiwan - Individual - Foreign tax relief and tax treaties

open_questions: Dividend taxation options were not verified in an opened source.
dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: separate 28% option (better than 40% less the capped credit for large dividends). Foreign: 20% IBT before credit; US 30% WHT (no treaty) would fully absorb it.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 21% WHT on dividends to non-residents, reducible by treaty (corporate summary, not opened).
dividends.treaty_network: About 35 comprehensive agreements; no income tax treaty with the US (the 2025 US legislation to extend treaty benefits was not verified as in force).
dividends.holding_company_notes: CIT 20% plus 5% profit retention tax on undistributed earnings.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Land value tax 1%-5.5% of assessed land value (lower rate for owner-occupied residences, not verified) and house tax 1%-4.8% of assessed value for non-commercial buildings (PwC); luxury tax 10% on certain goods.

inheritance.summary: Estate tax applies to the estate (estate basis) at 10% up to TWD 56.21 million, 15% to TWD 112.42 million and 20% above (inflation-indexed amounts from January 2025), after an exemption of TWD 13.33 million and deductions (e.g. TWD 560,000 per lineal descendant). For non-ROC nationals, and ROC nationals without habitual residence, only property located in Taiwan is taxed (Estate and Gift Tax Act Arts. 1 and 3). Gift tax: 10%-20% after a TWD 2.44 million annual exemption per donor, same scope rule.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Estate exemption TWD 13.33 million per decedent; TWD 560,000 deduction per child (plus TWD 560,000 per year under 18); spouse deduction TWD 5.53 million; funeral TWD 1.38 million. Gift: TWD 2.44 million per donor per year.
inheritance.important_exceptions: A foreign family pays estate tax only on Taiwan-situs assets (e.g. a Taiwan home and Taiwan shares). ROC nationals are taxed worldwide if domiciled in Taiwan within two years before death or resident more than 365 days in those two years (Art. 4).

sources.title: Estate and Gift Tax Act (English translation)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice, Laws & Regulations Database of the Republic of China (Taiwan)

inheritance.gift_tax: Gift tax 10% to TWD 28.11 million, 15% to 56.21 million, 20% above, after TWD 2.44 million per donor per year; non-nationals only on gifts of Taiwan property.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Nationality plus habitual residence (Art. 4): ROC nationals with a domicile in the two prior years or 365+ days of stay are taxed worldwide; non-nationals are always taxed on Taiwan property only.

residency.tax_residency_test: Foreign individuals: resident if present 183 days or more in a calendar year. ROC nationals with household registration are resident if domiciled and habitually residing, unless the 31-day rule applies.

routes.name: Investment-based resident certificate (ARC), Employment Gold Card, APRC
routes.requirements: Residence through investment in a Taiwan business, employment, or the Employment Gold Card for professionals; permanent residence (APRC) after qualifying years or for major investors (thresholds not verified).

corporate.summary: 20% CIT (income up to TWD 120,000 exempt); 5% profit retention tax on undistributed earnings; 12% corporate IBT, with proposals to raise it to 15% for Pillar Two groups.

income.name: Taiwan

income_tax.summary: Resident individuals pay progressive tax of 5% to 40% (top rate above TWD 4.98m), plus an alternative minimum tax. Employees' own social insurance is small: labor insurance 2.3%, employment insurance 0.2% (both capped at TWD 45,800 monthly insured salary) and national health insurance about 1.55% (insured-salary cap TWD 313,000). The Employment Gold Card exempts 50% of salary above TWD 3m for up to five years.

employment_deduction.note: Salary special deduction of up to TWD 218,000 a person (or the salary if lower).

income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed contribution rules (occupational union, higher NHI share) could not be found on any opened page (NHI and Bureau of Labor Insurance pages returned 403/404), so the self-employed rate is a PLACEHOLDER equal to the employee NHI share and is not verified; the real cost is probably higher because the employer's share falls on the self-employed person.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. Rates are for the 2025 return (filed 2026), the latest on PwC (page reviewed 20 August 2026); 2026 rates were not published. Allowance = personal exemption TWD 97,000 + standard deduction TWD 131,000 for a single filer; employees also get a salary special deduction of TWD 218,000 (not included). Alternative minimum tax: 20% on income above TWD 7.5m, payable if higher. Employee social insurance: labor insurance 11.5% x 20% = 2.3% and employment insurance 1% x 20% = 0.2% on insured salary up to TWD 45,800 a month (about TWD 1,145 a month), plus NHI 5.17% x 30% = 1.551% on insured salary up to TWD 313,000 a month; the recorded 1.551% rate and TWD 3,756,000 annual cap cover only NHI, so labor and employment insurance (small, capped) are excluded. Foreigners cannot join the labor pension.

sources.title: Employer costs in Taiwan 2026: labor insurance and more

open_questions: Self-employed social insurance rates not found.
Labor and employment insurance (max about TWD 1,145 a month) excluded from the employee rate; NHI cap of TWD 313,000 from a payroll blog (PwC says only 'various caps').
2026 tax-year brackets/allowances not yet published; 2025 figures used.
Deductibility of NHI premiums (the recorded 1.551%) not established: PwC deductions page mentions only labour and group insurance premiums (TWD 24,000 a person, itemised deductions).

regimes.name: Employment Gold Card: 50% exemption on salary above TWD 3m
regimes.description: Gold Card holders working in Taiwan for the first time may apply for a 50% exemption on annual salary above TWD 3 million for the first 5 years (Gold Card site); KPMG adds that the holder must reside more than 183 days in the year and not have been a Taiwan tax resident in the five prior years, and that the exempt portion is excluded from the AMT. exemption_threshold is TWD 3,000,000: only salary above it is 50% exempt. The card itself lets a professional stay and work 1 to 3 years with no sponsor or job offer.
regimes.duration_note: Five years of tax incentive; card issued for 1 to 3 years and presumably renewed (renewal not verified). Exemption applies only to the part of salary above TWD 3m, so there is no minimum income to qualify for the card's tax benefit.

sources.title: KPMG Flash Alert 2023-085: Taiwan Employment Gold Card tax incentive

open_questions: KPMG alert dates from 2023; conditions may have changed.
Whether the incentive applies to self-employment income (the text says 'salary') is not confirmed; applies_to is employment only.
